disposition_reason: Uranium-238 measured in 35 drinking well-water samples around the Semipalatinsk Nuclear Test Site (0.3 to 28.7 µg/L) and in Irtysh River water; adult annual effective doses derived.
disposition_locator: Abstract p. 309; Results p. 311; Table 2; Table 3 p. 314

study.design: cross-sectional environmental survey of drinking well water
study.origin: Kazakhstan, ten settlements around the Semipalatinsk Nuclear Test Site

period.as_reported: sample codes indicate collection in 1995 to 2005

study.method: alpha-particle spectrometry after anion-exchange separation with uranium-232 yield tracer
study.qa: yield tracer; isotope activity ratios reported with counting errors

findings.group: 35 wells in ten settlements around the Semipalatinsk Nuclear Test Site, Kazakhstan
findings.notes: Mass concentration converted by the authors from uranium-238 activity; water concentrations are not converted to µg/kg.
River surface water, comparison sample; sample count not restated in text.

regulatory_or_exposure: WHO proposed guideline of 15 µg/L uranium in drinking water as cited by the authors (3rd edition), p. 311
Annual effective dose to adults drinking 2 L/day: 1.0 to 18.7 µSv/y, below the 100 µSv/y WHO and IAEA reference value cited, Table 3 p. 314
non_numeric_findings: Uranium-235/uranium-238 activity ratio about 0.046 indicates natural uranium, attributed to rock weathering rather than test-site fallout (p. 311).
